Darunavir/cobicistat is indicated for use in combination with other antiretroviral agents in both treatment-naïve and treatment-experienced patients who do not have darunavir resistance-associated mutations. The recommended dose is one tablet (800 mg/150 mg) taken orally once daily with food. 2. In patients with a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of less than 70 mL/min, coadministration with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) is not recommended. 3. Darunavir/cobicistat is not recommended for use in patients with severe hepatic impairment. 4. Darunavir/cobicistat is not recommended for use in pregnant women due to significantly lower exposures of both darunavir and cobicistat during pregnancy. 5. HIV genotypic testing is recommended for treatment-experienced patients to guide therapy. 6. Darunavir/cobicistat is indicated for use in patients weighing at least 40 kg, with no darunavir resistance-associated substitutions. Safety and efficacy have not been established in patients weighing less than 40 kg. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions, such as hypotension. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of astemizole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to darunavir. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conivaptan also increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity characterized by peripheral vasospasm and ischemia of the extremities and other tissues. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine intranasally by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Darunavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters, which may increase the risk of ALT elevations due to significant increases in grazoprevir plasma concentrations. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. In extensive metabolizers, the eliglustat dose should be reduced from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are given concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 and BCRP metabolism. The duvelisib dose should be reduced to 15 mg twice daily when coadministered with cobicistat. 27. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity. 31.
